key_insight: A first-principles phonon-transport model gives the best and most physically consistent description of thermal transport in the studied AlGaN HEMT thin-film layers.
engineering_relevance: Reliable layer-level thermal conductivity models can support thermal management and buffer/transition-layer design in AlGaN HEMT stacks.
method: Compare three phonon-transport models, from a Debye approximation to DFT-derived harmonic and anharmonic phonon properties.
Include alloy, grain-boundary, and film-boundary scattering; fit boundary contributions to TDTR thermal conductivity measurements.
Establish intrinsic Umklapp-dominated transport before systematically adding other scattering mechanisms.
evidence_signal: Comparison with TDTR measurements favors the first-principles model, although the abstract reports no numerical errors or conductivity values.
watch_item: Boundary-scattering parameters are fitted to specific samples, so predictive accuracy for different thin-film microstructures requires validation.
paper_title: Thermal investigation of buffer and transition layers in AlGaN HEMT stacks
